# Advisory: CVE-2026-104854 / GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77

**Title:** Nx daemon and plugin worker sockets are accessible to other local users

**Summary:** Nx creates Unix domain sockets for its daemon and plugin workers in a shared temporary directory with default permissions. Other local users can connect to them. The daemon's `PROCESS_IN_BACKGROUND` request can load a named module and invoke its default export, so socket access becomes code execution inside the daemon process.

**Affected package:** `nx` (npm)

**Affected versions:**
- `>= 14.6.0, < 22.7.9`
- `>= 23.0.0, < 23.1.2`

**Patched versions:** 22.7.9 and 23.1.2

**Severity:** High, CVSS v4 base score 8.5
- Vector: `CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`
- Attack vector: Local; complexity: Low; requirements: None; privileges: Low; user interaction: None
- Impact: High on confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the vulnerable system; none on subsequent systems
- EPSS: 0.141% (3rd percentile). The advisory reports no known exploitation in the wild.

**CVE ID:** CVE-2026-104854

**Weaknesses:**
- CWE-269: Improper Privilege Management
- CWE-732: Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource

**Dates:**
- Published to GitHub Advisory Database (by the maintainer): Sep 11, 2026
- Published by NVD: Oct 2, 2026
- Published to GitHub Advisory Database: Oct 5, 2026
- Last updated: Oct 5, 2026

**Description:**
- The daemon and plugin workers communicate over Unix sockets in a subdirectory of the OS temp directory, created with default permissions that typically let all local users read and traverse it.
- The directory name is derived from a hash of the workspace path and process ID. It is unique but not secret.
- The socket connection has no authentication. Any local process that can reach it is trusted fully.
- A daemon request handler loads and invokes a module from a path supplied in the request. Absolute paths resolve regardless of lookup constraints, so a caller who can write a file anywhere they have access to (such as their home directory) can get the daemon to run it as the daemon's user.
- Other handlers expose workspace file contents, the project graph, and task hashes to unauthenticated callers.

**Exploitable conditions:**
- Another local account exists on the same host, such as a shared CI runner, shared build or development server, or a container running multiple uids.
- A daemon or plugin worker is running.
- No user interaction is required.
- Single-user machines, such as an ordinary laptop with one account, are not exposed.

**Workarounds and remediation:**
- **Upgrade (recommended):** `nx migrate 23.1.2`, or upgrade to 22.7.9 on the 22.x line.
- **Clean up after upgrading on shared machines:** run `nx reset` so sockets and directories created by older versions are removed rather than reused.
- **Set a private socket directory:** point `NX_SOCKET_DIR` at a directory you own with mode `0700`. The vulnerable versions already honor this variable.
- **Disable the daemon:** set `NX_DAEMON=false` to reduce the exposed surface. This does not cover plugin worker sockets, which are used during normal command runs even without the daemon, so it is not a full mitigation on its own.

**Credits:** The GitHub advisory lists Zyy0530, Str1ckl4nd, and 7thParkk as reporters. The description credits researchers at the University of Sydney: Liyi, Ziyue, Strick, Maurice, and Chenchen.

**References:**
- GitHub advisory: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/security/advisories/GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77
- NVD: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-104854
- Pull request: nrwl/nx#36370
- Commits: nrwl/nx@3298fd8, nrwl/nx@63e1abb, nrwl/nx@71c2253
- Release notes: https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/22.7.9 and https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/23.1.2

The release was published on **September 1, 2026** (the changelog lists it as 2026-09-01).

The fixes are all under "Fixes." The page doesn't label any of them as a security advisory, but the socket change is the closest to a security fix:

- **Socket access (security-related):** The daemon and plugin worker sockets now limit access to the owning user. The entry reads "restrict daemon and plugin worker socket access to the owning user," with issues #36586 and #36463 linked.
- **Windows path comparison:** Daemon workspace roots are now compared case-insensitively on Windows.
- **Node 26 crash:** Daemon log descriptors are closed after spawning, which avoids a crash on Node 26.
- **Shell-argument quoting:** A `quoteShellArg` helper was ported to support spawning without a shell.
- **Maven/Gradle analysis:** Maven and Gradle graph analysis no longer runs through a shell.

I've confirmed the advisory details and checked both repos' lockfiles and CI setup. Only the people-and-orgs repo is affected, and it needs a patch-level bump.

## GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77 (CVE-2026-104854)

**What it is:** In affected Nx versions, the background helper process (the "daemon") and the plugin worker processes talk over Unix sockets in a shared temp directory. That directory has default permissions and the sockets have no authentication. Any other local account on the same machine can connect. Through the daemon's `PROCESS_IN_BACKGROUND` request, that account can make the daemon load a file it wrote and run it as your user. It can also read workspace files, the project graph and task hashes. Severity is High (CVSS 4.0 score 8.5, local attack vector, low privileges needed). The advisory reports no known exploitation.

**Affected:** `nx` from 14.6.0 up to (not including) 22.7.9, and from 23.0.0 up to (not including) 23.1.2. **Fixed in:** 22.7.9 and 23.1.2. The fix is "restrict daemon and plugin worker socket access to the owning user" (nrwl/nx#36370).

**Dates:**

| Event | Date |
|---|---|
| 23.1.2 released | Aug 26, 2026 |
| 22.7.9 released | Sep 1, 2026 |
| Advisory published by Nx maintainers | Sep 11, 2026 |
| Published by NVD | Oct 2, 2026 |
| Added to the GitHub Advisory Database (last updated) | Oct 5, 2026 |

## Is each repo affected?

| Repo | Declared | Version in lockfile | Affected? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `financial-hq-ui` | `nx` 23.2.1 (`package.json:147`) | `nx@23.2.1` in `yarn.lock:9867`; all `@nx/*` packages are 23.2.1 | **No**: 23.2.1 is newer than the 23.1.2 fix |
| `people-and-orgs-ui-library` | `nx` 22.7.1 (`package.json:211`) | `nx@22.7.1` in `pnpm-lock.yaml:7568`; all `@nx/*` packages are 22.7.1 | **Yes**: it's in the 14.6.0 to before-22.7.9 range |

## Which environments matter

The issue only matters when **another local user account can reach the same temp directory while Nx is running**:
- **At risk:** shared CI runners where several jobs or users share one host, shared build or dev servers, and containers running processes under more than one user ID.
- **Not at risk:** single-user laptops and ephemeral single-tenant VMs. All workflows in both repos use GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners, which are fresh single-tenant VMs, so risk there is low. The `people-and-orgs-ui-library` Dockerfile build runs everything as root in one container, so risk is low there too.
- **Can't see from here:** `dev-image.yml` calls a shared template (`sportngin/se-actions-workflow-templates/.../build-dev-image.yml@main`), so I couldn't see which runner it uses. Also check whether anyone runs this repo on a shared dev box or a self-hosted runner. Those are the cases where the issue really applies.
- **Turning off the daemon doesn't fully help:** Nx turns the daemon off by default in CI, and neither repo sets `NX_DAEMON` or `useDaemonProcess`. But plugin worker sockets are still created during normal runs, so `NX_DAEMON=false` alone doesn't close the hole.

## Recommendations

**people-and-orgs-ui-library: upgrade to 22.7.9.** This is the smallest fix, a patch release within 22.7.x with no major-version migration.
- Bump `nx` and every `@nx/*` package (`angular`, `devkit`, `eslint`, `eslint-plugin`, `js`, `module-federation`, `plugin`, `workspace`) together to `22.7.9`. The simplest way is `pnpm exec nx migrate 22.7.9`, then `pnpm install`.
- Then check that `pnpm-lock.yaml` resolves `nx@22.7.9`, including the indirect `@nx/jest`, `@nx/rspack`, `@nx/web` and `@nx/webpack` entries.
- On any shared machine that ran the old version, run `nx reset` afterwards so the old sockets are deleted rather than reused.
- If the upgrade has to wait, a stopgap that already works in 22.7.1 is to set `NX_SOCKET_DIR` to a directory you own with mode `0700`.

**financial-hq-ui: no change needed.** 23.2.1 already contains the fix. Just make sure any future pin stays at 23.1.2 or later.

Sources:
- [GitHub Advisory GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-w3vv-58gj-gw77)
- [Nx 22.7.9 release](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/22.7.9)
- [Nx 23.1.2 release](https://github.com/nrwl/nx/releases/tag/23.1.2)
